key_insight: Layered verification catches different failures, but code-valid trading revisions can still conflict with human judgment or leave operational blind spots.
engineering_relevance: Deployed self-revising agents need deterministic safeguards, bounded reflection, human oversight, and interfaces that expose failures beyond gate checks.
method: Deployed an LLM trading agent against a live paper-brokerage account with nightly strategy self-revisions.
Combined deterministic risk and revision-integrity gates, bounded tool-restricted review, and human approval screens.
Compared 2.5 weeks of human-gated self-revisions with 5 weeks of auto-applied reflection revisions; chat remained human-gated.
evidence_signal: Code gates rejected no proposals; the human rejected two code-valid proposals and later removed 11 of 19 autonomously added rules at a median lag of eight days, while manually discovering incidents that passed every gate.
watch_item: This sequential, single-agent paper-trading deployment does not establish real-money safety or a causal advantage for either verification regime.
paper_title: AllPath: Layered Verification for a Deployed, Self-Revising LLM Trading Agent under Human-Gated and Autonomous Regimes
